Every induced component is a path, an isolate, or an even cycle. Consecutive pairing and a smaller bipartition side give a matching and cover of equal size componentwise. A new isolate contributes one to  $o(U_S)$  and zero to matching cost. Summing gives  $\nu(A[U_S])=(|U|-o(U_S))/2$  and the claimed saving. One deletion followed by one addition changes matching number by at most one in absolute value. Extending an optimal  $t$ -subset and shortening an optimal  $(t+1)$ -subset give the two directions of the frontier bound. The cost throughout is unit matching cardinality.Exactness of Theorem 3. At a fixed traversal cut, the identities of the live labels are known. The mask therefore needs only the selected live bits. The implementation charges  $s_i$  at the first endpoint, applies membership  $1-s_i$  at  $x_i$  and  $s_i$  at  $y_i$ , and forgets the decision only at the second endpoint. This works when  $y_i$  occurs first and when the endpoints lie in different components. Boundary merging retains both the live mask and  $t$ .The decisive cycle check is  $p_{\rm end}=h$ . If any vertex is absent, its zero resets parity, fixing the closed trace and charging exactly  $\lfloor L/2\rfloor$  on each circular present run of length  $L$ . If every vertex is present, the even cycle closes from either initial parity and both traces cost  $N/2$ . Thus every accepted trace for a fixed batch has its actual maximum matching cost. Histories with the same live mask, count, parity and cycle-start parity have identical continuations, so keeping one least-cost full-mask witness is valid. The bound of  $4(q+1)2^w$  states per layer and  $O(N(q+1)2^w)$  transitions follows, with polynomial bit and witness overhead. Each row reconstructs a batch. Reading the rows up to  $B$  also gives the fewest operations attaining the at-most- $B$  optimum.Physical wrapper. The global Counter checks the initial retained-owner degrees. Each post-swap check uses the edges of the affected owner component. Distinct owners make every subset and every prefix permitted. For a final tight cover  $C$ , take all  $b$  centres, the owners outside  $U_S$ , and the witnesses in  $U_S\setminus C$ . The cover and owner-degree conditions give induced maximum degree one and cardinality  $3b-|C|$ . The wrapper materializes this certificate for its best row. Every other row supplies the mask needed to reconstruct its certificate.Sharp physical families. In Theorem 4, component  $w_i,x_i,y_{i+1},z_{i+1}$  contributes exactly the indicator that operation  $i+1$  is selected. Its possible extra edge shares  $y_{i+1}$ . Hence every  $t$ -subset costs  $t$ . The two ears span each square module, and a vertex deletion destroys at most one cyclic join. For  $r=2$  the second intermodule edge survives, and for  $r=1$  the join is internal. The prescribed reversal gives width at most two, with width one at  $r=1$ .In Theorem 5, fixed absent boundary vertices separate the tiles. A selected tile changes  $P_4$  into an isolate and  $P_3$ , giving  $F(t)=2r-t$  at width one. The new vertex 5 remains adjacent to fixed vertex 4, so final isolation permits only the empty batch. Selecting all operations gives the  $11r$  physical certificate. The earlier mixed rule already achieves cost  $r$  by retaining cover vertex 4 and matching edge  $3\!-\!4$  in each selected tile. The subdivided cycle and four distinct attachments per owner establish two-connectivity after any one deletion. Both constructions have the claimed orders, bipartitions, degrees and minimum-cardinality initial omissions for every  $r\ge1$ .Budgeted hardness. Zero cost forces the final auxiliary graph to be edgeless, making final isolation automatic. In the attached reduction, selecting a label then forces its successor and hence its whole group. Selecting groups  $Z$  uses  $D|Z|$  operations and leaves cost  $|E(J-Z)|$ , so the first zero is exactly at  $D\tau(J)$ . The connected bridgeless normalization preserves the stated threshold and supplies two-connectivity of the physical construction. This proves NP-completeness for the budgeted decision and the conditional obstruction to a uniform polynomial full-frontier algorithm. Selecting all groups reaches zero on these instances, so the reduction leaves the unbudgeted primary-cost question open.Supplementary findings and limitsAn independent matching enumeration on  $C_6\sqcup C_4\sqcup P_3\sqcup K_1$ , with six cross-component replacements, checked all 64 batches and all 4,608 legal traversals.
